kandidaty.zagolovok: [AINews] Riemann Hypothesis proved...twice independently
kandidaty.tekst:
Within a few hours of each other (timeline), two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics (Scientific American).

Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code (1.3GB worth, ~250,000 page equivalent) rather than a full paper. Elliot Glazer confirms that the formalized statement is GRH and puts the chance of a Lean bug well under 1%. So if it finishes compiling with no extra axioms, it is probably correct, and no human will ever have read all of it…

…prompting Alessandro Masullo to release his 940 page, 100% human, work in progress proof he had been working on for the last 12 years (and had been undergoing secret manual review and revision per Kevin Hartnett).

This is the third in the trilogy of frontier math breakthroughs, following from the Navier Stokes solutions and the Quasi-Riemann bounding, but it doesn’t feel over. OpenAI's September Navier-Stokes claim is still the cautionary tale: critics argued that its Lean proof did not match the natural-language result. Both AI-claimed Millennium Prize results will take years to verify.

Apart from the incredible accomplishment of the most famous problem in mathematics, one cannot miss the contrast that the AI-written solution is probably correct but incomprehensible, and the other solution is probably technically incorrect but understandable.

Sponsored by Agentfield.AI

Open models are ready. Most coding harnesses aren’t. On DeepSWE, CodeAF finished #1 of ten on the same open model, ahead of Claude Code, at the lowest cost per fix.

Try CodeAF!

As Levent eloquently put it: “Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.”

This also ties into other AI themes we’ve covered on the podcast and on this newsletter:

The nature of Slop: Levent says “I am presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics. It being obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of "slop", I decided to only present Lean.” One of the key tenets of the No Slop Manifesto is that you should understand what you ship (“Slop is when we put less effort into producing something than we ask the consumer to spend understanding it.”). And yet, this giant pile of Lean is verifiably correct and is incredibly significant in human history. Should we have delayed its release by a decade simply because we didn’t understand every single bit of it?

Weak to Strong alignment: the typical experience of using agents is Strong to Weak - we are general intelligences guiding not-as-smart AI to do things we know how to do well. We also often expect AI to automate most work “within distribution”, and expect it to run into more trouble at the limits of capability where the “centaur” pattern of human-AI-collaboration is required. Levent’s lived experience is the opposite - col

Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of [Generalized Riemann Hypothesis], and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. kandidaty.zagolovok: Quoting Levent Alpöge
kandidaty.tekst:
I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis. In fact, the method easily extends much further, resolving the so-called Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, and I expect, with more time, the Extended Riemann Hypothesis too. Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions. It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater. [...]

Claude and I have had a great time together with such breadth in recent months, but this time Claude far outpaced me near the finish line. No, Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.

— Levent Alpöge, alpo.ge/remark.pdf

kandidaty.zagolovok: Agent Anomaly Detection: Safeguarding agents across other clouds
kandidaty.tekst: Agent Anomaly Detection now monitors ADK agents running across AWS, Azure, or on-premises by analyzing their traces and logs in your Google Cloud project. By ingesting OpenTelemetry-formatted data through the Telemetry API, it evaluates full conversations for behavioral drift without needing access to the agent's underlying runtime. This enables security teams to detect risks like rogue behaviors, tool misuse, and resource exhaustion across multi-cloud environments.

kandidaty.zagolovok: Check what your AI agents do before they do it, with Semantic governance policies
kandidaty.tekst: Semantic governance policies enable developers to govern AI agents by evaluating every proposed tool call inline before execution. Operating via Agent Gateway, the policy engine checks each action against user intent and plain-language rules to prevent unauthorized data sharing and prompt injection attacks. Developers can easily attach natural-language constraints to their agents and monitor auditable verdicts through Cloud Logging.

kandidaty.tekst: When building a custom enterprise UI on top of Gemini Enterprise's :streamAssist API, developers must manually implement three core authentication layers. These include authenticating users or workloads via Google Identity or Workforce/Workload Identity Federation, managing third-party 3-legged OAuth (3LO) for Federated Connectors through the Keystore, and configuring on-demand per-tool OAuth for custom ADK agents using Vertex AI Agent Engine and GCP Auth Manager.

kandidaty.zagolovok: Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Tunix and Gemma 4 on Google TPUs
kandidaty.tekst: This post walks developers through training a multi-turn, tool-using LLM agent using Tunix and Gemma 4 on Cloud TPUs. By leveraging agentic Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and asynchronous vLLM rollouts, the approach significantly improves complex reasoning and tool compliance in interactive environments.

kandidaty.zagolovok: Distributed LLM Training Across Metros: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText
kandidaty.tekst: Streaming DiLoCo in MaxText enables developers to efficiently train large language models across geographically distributed TPU slices by streaming parameter fragments instead of synchronizing full models at every step. This approach slashes cross-slice communication volume by over 60× and eliminates network stalls, allowing seamless multi-datacenter scaling without degrading model convergence or quality.

kandidaty.zagolovok: How AI is helping scientists uncover new leads for understanding and treating neurodegenerative diseases—and the brain r
kandidaty.tekst:
@OpenAI: How AI is helping scientists uncover new leads for understanding and treating neurodegenerative diseases—and the brain research behind our collaboration with @perturbai_tx and @scrippsresearch:

Цитирует @OpenAI: GPT-Rosalind surfaced a new lead for drug discovery: could restoring cholesterol transport protect neurons from degeneration?

DCTN1 is a gene linked to Perry syndrome, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. In mouse-brain data, disrupting it increased expression of genes involved in making cholesterol. GPT-Rosalind suggested a possible explanation: cholesterol may not be reaching where neurons need it.

That gives scientists a specific mechanism to test and, if confirmed, a direction for developing new treatments for neurodegenerative disorders.

With @perturbai_tx and @scrippsresearch, a team of thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents worked in parallel, connecting gene-expression results from millions of mouse brain cells with scientific literature in just 32 minutes. We’re now expanding this collaboration to identify new drug targets.

https://openai.com/index/scaling-ai-research-for-complex-biological-data/

kandidaty.zagolovok: Google recently announced Loop, its new self-improving AI agent that can autonomously work toward a given goal. Loop is
kandidaty.tekst:
@testingcatalog: Google recently announced Loop, its new self-improving AI agent that can autonomously work toward a given goal. 

Loop is internally called Jitro; interestingly, that was the exact name for Jules v2. 

Here is how it works 👀

1. Users start creating a Workspace by connecting it to a selected Github project and adding basic information. 

2. Users can create loops manually or select ones that are already predefined (ex., Harden Application Security)

"Custom Loops" can be created via a prompt or by manually filling in the Loop title, icon, and objective. 

> "Loops are mid- to long-term objectives for Stitch Loop to continuously work toward. They can range from highly specific to broad, but should always be something code can achieve," says the description. 

3. Users can connect additional context in the form of Integrations, Files, Links, or additional repositories.

More than 100 integrations are available there, including services like Jira, Linear, Datadog, Sentry, Notion, Snowflake, Salesforce, Intercom, Discord, Slack, Figma, and many others. 

Custom MCPs are supported as well. 

4. After creating a workspace, Loop will start digging into your project details and generate its own Skills about the product and product metrics. 

These Skills will live in a separate tab and can be edited in the UI in Markdown. 

5. When the Workspace is ready, Loop will suggest metrics and goals based on its own research. Users can convert these suggestions into loops right away. 

When a Loop is created, it appears as a running process in the main UI. 

6. When a Loop is finished, users will see a list of suggestions for every loop, along with a number associated with a target metric and progress status. 

Example Loop:
- Goal - Scale Telegram community contributions.
- KPIs - community members, registered contributors, active members. 

A high-level goal would be broken down into sub-KPIs. When users open a dedicated Loop page, all these KPIs will be visible on the dashboard.

Below, Users will see a list of Tasks, Skills, and Activity tabs. 

Example Task:
- Telegram channel lacks discussion threads and a dedicated bot.

Each task has a detailed description, labels, and the date when it was updated. Below, users will see tabs for Solutions, Activity, and Evidence. 

Activity appears as a summary describing what happened, what was done, and the general Timeline. 

Evidence contains links to where Loop pulled the context behind this Task. In my example case, it refers to the TestingCatalog website and the Telegram channel from which it pulled all the numbers. 

Example Solution: 
- Dedicated Telegram Bot API intake bot with editorial triage webhook (implementation task). 

This task is an implementation task that has a clear description, Impact, scope, and Risk labeled. 

Users can start the task right from this page to begin solution development via Gemini. 

When the task is done, users can review its progress and status and monitor its im
